article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Evening Brief
article.dek: The Sunday-night inactives are in, Atlanta moved to -3.5, and all three cards re-dealt onto Monday night — with the Value lane empty.

items.headline: Sunday-night inactives: Flowers and Humphrey play, Vorhees is out
paragraphs: The inactive lists are in for Sunday night in Atlanta, and the questionable tags broke both ways. Ravens guard Andrew Vorhees (foot) went from questionable to OUT, so Baltimore starts without both its center Cam Jurgens (concussion) and a starting guard in front of Tyler Huntley. Already ruled out: Lamar Jackson (ankle), Trey Hendrickson, plus Elijah Sarratt and Aeneas Peebles.

The good news for Baltimore: wide receiver Zay Flowers (foot) and cornerback Marlon Humphrey are both ACTIVE after limited practices all week. Huntley starts at quarterback. For Atlanta: edge rusher Za'Darius Smith (concussion) and linebacker Christian Harris are out, while left tackle Jake Matthews (groin) is active for his 200th consecutive start, along with Divine Deablo and Samson Ebukam.

The market has fully digested the Huntley news. Atlanta is -3.5 on both DraftKings and FanDuel now, with the Falcons -172 on the moneyline at FanDuel. If your book is still hanging a different number on this game, tap Check: type in the line and price you can actually bet and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator for a verdict on YOUR number.
items.takeaway: The news is in the price. Your edge is the number in front of you.

items.headline: Quarterback check: the board matches the news
paragraphs: The app's quarterback feed is fresh and matches the news. Tyler Huntley is listed as Baltimore's expected starter for Sunday night. Michael Penix starts for Atlanta. Tomorrow night it's Josh Allen for Buffalo and Matthew Stafford for the Rams.
That's the check that matters on a Sunday evening: when the board agrees with the news, there's no stale number to fade and no rumor to chase. Bet the slate, not the rumor.
items.takeaway: The board's quarterbacks match the news. Nothing to fade, nothing to chase.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate is on Buffalo — and it's a dog
paragraphs: Hit Rate means the supported pick the app thinks is most likely to win — win probability first, value second. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate. Tonight it's Buffalo on the moneyline at +150 on DraftKings, visiting the Rams on Monday night at 8:15 p.m. ET.

The honest number: the app evaluates Buffalo's chance at 38.6% against a 40.0% breakeven at +150 — just short, reliability MEDIUM. The app's raw read likes Buffalo better than the market does, but liking a team and the price paying you are two different things. The card chases the win, not the value; tonight the win is a dog and the price barely misses.
If your book has Buffalo better than +150, that's a better number than the card; if it's worse, tap Check and run your price before you decide.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate chases the win, not the value. Tonight the win is a dog.

items.headline: Balanced stays with Buffalo; Value finds nothing
paragraphs: Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor. It's Buffalo +3.5 at -115 on DraftKings. The app's evaluated chance is 49.8% against a 53.5% breakeven — short, reliability MEDIUM.

Value is always the model's +EV play, and tonight the Value lane is empty: no offer on the board satisfies the lane's contract. Some evenings the board's honest answer is nothing. That's the report, not a failure — a quiet board is information too.
items.takeaway: Two cards on Buffalo, both thin; the honest third card is empty.

items.headline: How to use this before Monday night
paragraphs: Every news item above closes the loop the same way. The board refreshes every morning and evening. When your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, or the line moved since the board last refreshed, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

One mechanics note: +150 means every $1 you risk wins $1.50; -115 means every $1.15 you risk wins $1. That's price mechanics, not a stake — the app sizes your actual stake from your bankroll and your staking setting, which is deliberately conservative.
items.takeaway: Report the news first, then use it: Check is how news becomes a number.

items.headline: Closing line value — beating the close
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine you bet a team at -2.5 on Tuesday, and by kickoff the line has moved to -4.5. You 'beat the close' by 2 points — you got a better price than the final market. That's called closing line value, or CLV.

Beating the close doesn't mean the bet wins — the game still has to be played. But over dozens of bets, consistently beating the close is the sharpest track record there is, because the closing line is the market's best guess after all the information is in. Losing bets that beat the close are usually good bets; winning bets that got the worst of the number are usually lucky ones. Our Fade rule needs a real split plus corroboration before it becomes a play; when a real one qualifies, this section will say so plainly.
items.takeaway: You can't control the bounce, but you can control the price — beating the close is the number that follows you.

items.headline: Atlanta moved to -3.5 on both books
paragraphs: This morning DraftKings had Atlanta at -3.0 while FanDuel sat at -3.5. During the day DraftKings joined FanDuel: both books now show Falcons -3.5, with the moneyline around -172 to -175 and the DraftKings total at 44.5. The board caught the move — the market snapshot was fresh when we read it.

The Huntley news is fully priced now. If your book is still hanging Falcons -3.0, that's a stale number in your favor; if it's past -3.5, the value went the other way. Either way, tap Check with the line you can actually bet.
items.takeaway: The price moved, the news didn't. Shop it.

items.headline: All three cards re-dealt onto Monday night
paragraphs: This morning's cards — Denver, Minnesota, San Francisco — were today's games and are off the board now. All three evening cards sit on Monday night's Bills-Rams game: Hit Rate and Balanced both on Buffalo, and the Value lane empty.

When the card changes, the play changes — yesterday's numbers are yesterday's. The model's raw read leans Buffalo by about two points while the market has the Rams -3.5, yet the evaluator's final numbers still land short of breakeven on both cards. Check your book's number against tonight's card, not this morning's.
items.takeaway: When the card changes, the play changes. Check your book's number.

items.headline: Shop the Monday-night number tonight
paragraphs: Sunday night kicks off in minutes, so the next prices that matter are Monday night's: Buffalo +150 on the moneyline and +3.5 on the spread at DraftKings. Lines for tomorrow's game can move overnight — if you like the Bills side of either card, shop it tonight rather than at kickoff.
Monday-night inactives land about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, and tomorrow's briefs will have them. Until then, your book's line is the only line that matters — run it through Check.
items.takeaway: Shop the price before the game, not during it.
